title: Pranavi Urs Honoured at NDTV IGPL Pro-Am After Historic Asian Games Golf Gold
excerpt: Days after becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold, the 23-year-old received a standing ovation at the NDTV IGPL Golf Pro-Am, where a ₹1 crore cash prize was announced for her.
body:
• Pranavi Urs, 23, became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold in golf, finishing at 15-under 265 at the Kasugai Country Club East Course in Aichi-Nagoya.
  • She recovered from a triple bogey on the third hole of the final round with birdies on the sixth, 10th and 13th, signing an even-par 70 to edge China's Yin Ruoning and Singapore's Shannon Tan by one stroke.
  • Urs also anchored India to its first-ever women's team medal at the Games, a silver, alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar; former India captain Kapil Dev praised her "nerves of steel and tremendous belief."
  • Days after the win, Urs received a standing ovation at the NDTV IGPL Golf Pro-Am in India, where fellow champions Shiv Kapur and Leander Paes congratulated her and Anurag Thakur announced a ₹1 crore cash prize for the champion.

Pranavi Urs walked into the NDTV IGPL Golf Pro-Am to a standing ovation from India's golfing community — and walked out with a ₹1 crore cash prize announced by Anurag Thakur. The felicitation came days after the 23-year-old from Mysuru scripted history at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold at the continental showpiece.

The honour capped a week built on composure: at the Kasugai Country Club East Course, Urs steadied herself after an early triple bogey to sign an even-par 70 and finish at 15-under 265, one stroke clear of the chasing pair.

Context & Background

Urs began the final round with a three-stroke advantage over Singapore's Shannon Tan, but the past looked ready to repeat itself on the par-4 third hole. Trapped in a bunker, she needed two attempts to escape and walked off with a triple bogey that wiped out her lead and handed China's Yin Ruoning — a six-time LPGA winner and the 2023 Women's PGA Championship major champion — the advantage.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2106387634700562849

Instead of folding, Urs birdied the sixth for breathing space, added another on the 10th to draw level, and sank the defining putt on the 13th after it appeared to circle the rim. Five closing pars later, she had history. "I just knew it was either a putt to win or it was a putt to force a playoff," she said. "All I wanted to do was obviously hole the putt."

The gold ended a 24-year wait for India's next individual Asian Games golf title since Shiv Kapur's 2002 Busan triumph — only the country's fourth golf title overall — and went one better than Hangzhou 2023, where Aditi Ashok's silver was India's first women's individual medal and Urs finished fourth.

Urs also anchored India to silver in the women's team event at 14-under 546 — the country's first medal in the format — behind China's 22-under 538, with Chinese Taipei taking bronze. Aditi closed with a three-under 67 to finish 14th individually; Diksha Dagar tied for 18th.

Impact & Analysis

The tributes underlined what the double-medal haul means for Indian golf. Kapil Dev, the former India cricket captain who now heads the Professional Golf Tour of India, said the medals were "moments of immense pride for India and Indian golf," adding: "These medals are a reflection of the talent, determination and hard work of our players and of the growing strength of women's golf in our country. Pranavi showed nerves of steel and tremendous belief to win the Gold Medal for India."

Urs arrived in Nagoya already a barrier-breaker: her 2025 IGPL Invitational win in Mumbai made her the first Indian woman to win a professional event in a mixed-gender field. On the Ladies European Tour she has repeatedly knocked on the door of a first title, including third place at the 2024 Andalucia Costa Del Sol Open de España. Her summary of the week was characteristically direct: "That's always the goal — to always be the first one to do anything. The first will always be the first."

"Pranavi showed nerves of steel and tremendous belief to win the Gold Medal for India."

— Kapil Dev, former India captain and Professional Golf Tour of India president

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, Urs' win lands in a sport where the community's presence keeps growing — from US and UK junior circuits to collegiate tours. A first Asian Games women's golf gold gives those pathways a visible landmark.

What's Next

Urs does not rest long. She heads to the Hero Women's Indian Open later this month on home soil among the favourites, with the gold adding momentum to her chase for a maiden Ladies European Tour title. With Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar alongside her in the team silver, India has a three-strong core for its next Olympic cycle.
